intro: You use numbers from 0 to 20 every day: to give your age, a phone number, a room number, a quantity or a simple price. They are the base of all other numbers.
objectifs: Say, write and spell the numbers from 0 to 20 easily.
Hear and say the -teen numbers with the right stress.
Say a phone number digit by digit, with “oh” and “double”.
Use numbers with plural nouns and do small sums out loud.

sections.titre: 0 to 12: words to learn by heart
texte: The numbers from 0 to 12 have no rule: each one is a different word. Learn the spelling too, because some are not written the way they sound (eight, two, one).
“One” sounds like /wʌn/, the same as “won”, with a w sound at the start. “Two” sounds like /tuː/, the same as “too” and “to”: the w is silent.

lignes: tongue between the teeth, breathe out

texte: From 13 to 19, add -teen to the number. Three numbers change: three → thirteen, five → fifteen, eight → eighteen (only one t, not “eightteen”). Four keeps its u: fourteen.

When you say the number alone, stress -TEEN: thirTEEN, fourTEEN. This helps people hear the difference from thirty and forty (30, 40), which are stressed at the start (THIRty). You will see them in lesson 20.
20 is “twenty” /ˈtwenti/. The word “teenager” comes from these numbers: a person from 13 to 19 years old.
exemples: Room thirteen is on the first floor.

texte: There are several ways to say 0. “Zero” is the general word (temperatures, maths, and almost everywhere in American English).
In a phone number, a room number or a bus number, British people often say “oh”, like the letter O. In football, British English says “nil”: two-nil (2-0). In tennis, 0 is “love”.
In English, say a phone number digit by digit: 06 12 = “oh six, one two”. Make a small pause between the groups.
When two digits are the same, British people often say “double”: 77 = “double seven”. Americans usually say “seven seven”. For three of the same digit, say “triple” or each digit.
To ask: “What's your phone number?”. To check: “Can you repeat that, please?”.
exemples: My number is oh-seven-nine, double four, one-six.
Say: oh-four-seven-two, one-five, double eight, three-oh.
sections.note: American English says “call me at…”; British English says “call me on…”.

sections.titre: Numbers with nouns and small sums
texte: After a number bigger than 1, the noun takes -s: one book, two books, twelve students. After “one”, the noun stays singular. The number itself never takes -s: “three apples”, never “threes apples”.
“A” and “one” both mean 1, but “one” makes the number important: I have one brother (only one, not two).
For sums: + plus, − minus, × times, ÷ divided by, = is / equals. The verb is singular: Two plus two is four.

lignes: Twenty divided by two is ten.

exemples: I have two sisters and one brother.
There are eighteen students in the class.

formule: 0 zero · 1 one · 2 two … 12 twelve · 13–19: number + -teen (thirteen, fifteen, eighteen) · 20 twenty
prononciation: Alone, a -teen number is stressed at the end: thirTEEN /θɜːˈtiːn/. Before a noun the stress can move (THIRteen students), but the long /iː/ of -teen is always clear.
“Three” /θriː/: put your tongue between your teeth and breathe out. Don't say “tree” or “free”.
“Eight” /eɪt/ sounds like “ate”: the gh is silent.
“Twelve” /twelv/ and “twenty” /ˈtwenti/: say the w after the t. In American English, “twenty” often sounds like /ˈtweni/.
In a phone number, your voice goes up a little at the end of each group and down at the end of the number.
erreurs: After a number bigger than 1, the noun takes -s.
My number is zero six, twelve, thirty-four…
My number is oh six, one two, three four…
Say phone numbers digit by digit.
In sums, the verb is singular (is / equals).

dialogue.contexte: At the reception of a hotel in Brussels, a guest arrives and gives her details.
lignes: Good evening. Can I have your name, please?
A polite way to ask a name.
Yes, it's Grace Owona. I have a reservation for two nights.
Thank you. And what's your phone number?
It's oh-six, double seven, one-three, one-four, one-nine.
Sorry, is that thirteen or thirty?
She repeats it digit by digit.
Perfect. You're in room eleven, on the second floor. Here's your key.
Thank you. And what time is breakfast?

mots: a word or sign like 1, 2 or 3
My number has double five in it.
two of the same digit, one after the other
Can you count to twenty in English?
a person from 13 to 19 years old

exercices.consigne: Each word has a mistake. Write it correctly.
Write the sum and the answer in English.
items: Eighteen divided by three is six.

exercices.consigne: Write how a British speaker says this number (digit by digit, with “oh” and “double”).
items: oh six, one two, double five, oh nine
oh seven, nine eight, three oh, double one

exercices.consigne: Each sentence has one mistake. Write it correctly (numbers in letters).
items: There are eleven player in a football team.
There are eleven players in a football team.

exercices.consigne: Write three true sentences with numbers from 0 to 20: your age or a relative's age, the number of people in your family, a number (bus, room, floor…).
items: My niece is nine. There are five people in my family. I take bus number twelve to work.

a_retenir: 0 to 12: different words to learn (one /wʌn/, two /tuː/, eight /eɪt/, twelve).
13 to 19: number + -teen, with thirteen, fifteen, eighteen (one t).
Zero: zero (general), oh (phone, room), nil (British football).
Phone numbers: digit by digit, “double” for two of the same digit.
Number > 1 + plural noun: two books. Sums use “is”: Two plus two is four.
